exposure: elective induction of labour at 41 weeks
low-risk women with uncomplicated singleton late-term pregnancy
outcome: Composite adverse outcome (perinatal death, Apgar score 5' < 7, NICU admission, meconium aspiration syndrome)
Composite severe adverse perinatal outcome (all above with Apgar score 5' < 4 instead of < 7)
cohort: 3642 low-risk women with uncomplicated singleton late-term pregnancy
finding: In this cohort study of low-risk women, there was no significant difference in adverse perinatal outcomes between induction of labour at 41 weeks and expectant management until 42 weeks.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were comparable between induction of labour at 41 weeks (10.5%) and expectant management until 42 weeks (8.9%).
